payload.title: Emerging Python Operator DSLs: Triton, CuTeDSL, Mojo Overview
payload.summary: A survey of emerging Python-based domain-specific languages for GPU kernel development, comparing Triton, CuTeDSL, TileLang, cuTile, Mojo, and other frameworks across abstraction levels, ecosystems, and performance characteristics.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.gist: DSL (Domain-Specific Language) refers to languages designed for specific domains (HTML/SQL/regex).

sections.heading: 2. Triton
sections.gist: AI kernel computations are highly regular — tiling alone yields good performance.

sections.heading: 3. Helion
sections.gist: A Tensor-oriented DSL with **higher abstraction than Triton**.

sections.heading: 5. TileLang
sections.gist: Built on TVM thread-level primitives with **three programming interfaces**: explicit memory declaration, explicit thread control, or hands-off mode.

sections.heading: 6. Apache TVM
sections.gist: A comprehensive deep learning framework providing DSL operator authoring.

sections.heading: 7. Mojo
sections.gist: Chris Lattner's vision to build an **AI infrastructure company** serving various hardware vendors toward AI democratization.

sections.heading: 9. Tiramisu
sections.gist: Inspired by Halide but more oriented toward **deeply nested loops, complex scheduling structures, and polyhedral analysis**.

sections.heading: 10. NVIDIA cuTile
sections.gist: NVIDIA's DSL designed to **counter Triton**, directly competing with it.

sections.heading: 11. Performance Comparison (tritonbench)
sections.gist: **Test environment**: GPU H20 SXM 96GB x1, CPU 16-core, Memory 154 GB.

sections.heading: 12. Other Notable Projects
sections.gist: - **HazyResearch/ThunderKittens** ("tk"): Framework-oriented with DSL-style kernel definition and schedule API; strong performance, C++.
